prompts.display_text: Pin the Kirtland Temple, dedicated in 1836.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on the Kirtland Temple in Ohio, the first temple of the Restoration, dedicated in 1836.
prompts.citation: Kirtland Temple page, ChurchofJesusChrist.org, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: The Saints sacrificed to build the Kirtland Temple, which was dedicated on March 27, 1836 (D&C 109). One week later Jesus Christ appeared to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery there, followed by Moses, Elias and Elijah, who restored priesthood keys (D&C 110). Community of Christ cared for the temple for decades until stewardship passed to the Church in March 2024.

prompts.display_text: Pin an island nation (Australia aside) that has at least one dedicated temple.
prompts.text_original: An island country, not counting Australia, with at least one dedicated temple (as of November 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Island nations with dedicated temples stretch from the United Kingdom and New Zealand (both 1958) to Samoa, Tonga, Fiji and Cape Verde. Hispaniola is shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti, and both count. Territories such as Puerto Rico, Guam and Tahiti are excluded.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Tokyo Japan (1980), Fukuoka Japan (2000), Sapporo Japan (2016) and others.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Hamilton New Zealand (1958), Auckland New Zealand (2025).

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Manila Philippines (1984), Cebu City Philippines (2010), Urdaneta Philippines (2024) and others.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London England (1958), Preston England (1998).

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Nuku'alofa Tonga (1983).

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: Apia Samoa (1983).

answers.name: Dominican Republic
answers.fact: Santo Domingo Dominican Republic (2000).

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Suva Fiji (2000).

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Taipei Taiwan (1984).

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: Port-au-Prince Haiti (2019).

answers.name: Cape Verde
answers.fact: Praia Cape Verde (2022).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the US with 4 or more temples announced but not yet being built.
prompts.text_original: A country outside the United States with four or more temples announced but not yet under construction, as of November 2026.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology cross-checked with the Church's official temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Recent prophets announced temples faster than they can be built. As of November 2026 these countries each have at least four announced temples where work has not started.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Ten announced on the official list, including Cancún, Toluca, Culiacán and Reynosa.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: At least five announced, including Florianópolis, Goiânia, Vitória and Campo Grande.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: At least five announced, including Cusco, Piura, Chiclayo and Chorrillos.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Five announced: Tuguegarao City, Santiago, Iloilo, Laoag and San Jose del Monte.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Four announced: Eket, Calabar, Abuja and Uyo.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country Spencer W. Kimball dedicated for missionary work, from Central America to Poland.
prompts.text_original: A country Spencer W. Kimball dedicated or rededicated for the preaching of the gospel, as an Apostle or as Church President.
prompts.citation: Church History Department, Global Histories country chronologies, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Spencer W. Kimball opened much of Latin America to missionary work while in the Twelve, dedicating Central America in 1952 and several Andean nations in the 1960s. As Church President he rededicated Poland in 1977.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: November 16, 1952, Guatemala City: dedicated Central America for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: June 1, 1967, La Paz: dedicated Bolivia for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: May 1966, Bogota: began formal preaching, dedicated the country and organized the Colombia Branch.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: October 9, 1965: dedicated Ecuador on the Panecillo hilltop in Quito.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: 1952: opened the Central American Mission and dedicated Central America, including Honduras.

answers.name: Poland
answers.fact: August 24, 1977, Warsaw: as Church President, rededicated Poland.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country with a city or province where the New Testament places a named Roman official, the emperor aside.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country with a city or province where the New Testament places a named Roman official, the emperor aside
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: Roman officials appear across the New Testament. Pilate, Felix and Festus governed Judea, Gallio ruled at Corinth, and Sergius Paulus believed at Paphos (Acts 13:7). The centurion Julius escorted Paul from Caesarea past Sidon and Crete to Malta, where Publius hosted him, and on to Rome by way of Puteoli (Acts 27-28). Luke dates the Nativity by Cyrenius, governor of Syria.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Pilate judged Jesus at Jerusalem, and Felix, Festus, Cornelius and Claudius Lysias served at Caesarea (Luke 23:1; Acts 10:1; 23:26; 24:27).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Gallio was deputy of Achaia at Corinth, and the centurion Julius held Paul's ship at Fair Havens in Crete (Acts 18:12; 27:8-11).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Sergius Paulus, the deputy at Paphos, believed when Elymas was struck blind (Acts 13:7).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: The centurion Julius brought Paul ashore at Puteoli and on to Rome (Acts 28:13-16).

answers.name: Malta
answers.fact: Publius, the chief man of the island, hosted Paul for three days (Acts 28:7).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: The centurion Julius changed ships at Myra, a city of Lycia (Acts 27:5-6).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Luke dates the birth of Jesus by Cyrenius, governor of Syria; the New Testament names the province, not a city (Luke 2:2).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Julius let Paul visit his friends when the ship touched at Sidon (Acts 27:3).
